docs.text: CWL MCP Extension cwl-mcp-extension defines a small CWL extension for attaching MCP tool metadata to a CWL Process without duplicating standard CWL execution semantics. This repository is a work in progress. Contributions, feedback, and discussion are welcome. Scope The extension introduces two records: mcp:Tool mcp:ToolAnnotations These records are intended for use in CWL metadata, typically under hints , to provide agent-facing guidance for deriving an MCP Tool from a CWL Process . Namespace The canonical namespace URI for this extension is https://eoap.github.io/cwl-mcp-extension# . cwlmcp is the recommended prefix. Prefixes are aliases; the namespace URI is the actual identifier. EOAP currently hosts the namespace because EOAP maintains this extension. The project intentionally does not claim an unregistered w3id.org namespace at this stage. A neutral persistent namespace may be adopted later if the extension moves toward broader CWL community standardization. Canonical Example cwlVersion: v1.2 class: Workflow $namespaces: mcp: https://eoap.github.io/cwl-mcp-extension# hints: mcp:Tool: annotations: readOnlyHint: false destructiveHint: false idempotentHint: false openWorldHint: true References MCP specification (2026-07-28): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28 MCP Tools section: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools Tool annotations background: https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-03-16-tool-annotations/ Next Reading Specification CWL to MCP Crosswalk Authoring Guide Design Principles

docs.text: Authoring Guide Minimal Pattern Attach mcp:Tool metadata under hints : $namespaces: mcp: https://eoap.github.io/cwl-mcp-extension# hints: mcp:Tool: annotations: readOnlyHint: true Authoring Tips Set name only when the default normalized CWL id is not good enough. Reuse CWL label and doc unless you need MCP-specific presentation text. Keep useWhen and doNotUseWhen concise and action-oriented. Treat aliases as discovery aids, not as alternate identifiers. Avoid restating CWL inputs or outputs inside mcp:Tool . Example $namespaces: mcp: https://eoap.github.io/cwl-mcp-extension# hints: mcp:Tool: name: buffer_geometry aliases: - buffer a geometry - expand an area of interest useWhen: | Use when the user needs to expand a point or polygon into a buffered area. doNotUseWhen: | Do not use when exact geometry preservation is required. annotations: readOnlyHint: true destructiveHint: false idempotentHint: true openWorldHint: false

CWL remains the source of truth for input/output typing. MCP display precedence is title , then annotations.title , then name . Generators may keep richer provenance metadata than is emitted into the MCP Tool object.

docs.text: Design Principles Minimal Surface Area The extension should remain intentionally small and should only model metadata that standard CWL does not already express. Clear Precedence Explicit mcp:Tool values override derived values, but only for MCP-facing presentation and discovery behavior. No Semantic Duplication Inputs, outputs, execution requirements, and workflow topology belong to CWL and should not be mirrored inside the extension. Safe Interpretation Annotation fields are hints. They do not grant permission, replace policy, or guarantee runtime behavior. Canonical Aggregation The extension should have one stable entrypoint so validators, generators, and downstream tooling can resolve the record set consistently.

docs.text: CWL MCP Extension Specification Overview This extension introduces two records: mcp:Tool mcp:ToolAnnotations These records are intended for use in CWL metadata, typically under hints , to provide agent-facing guidance for deriving an MCP Tool from a CWL Process . Namespace The canonical namespace URI for this extension is https://eoap.github.io/cwl-mcp-extension# . mcp is the recommended prefix. Prefixes are aliases; the namespace URI is the actual identifier. EOAP hosts the namespace because EOAP currently maintains this extension. The project intentionally does not claim an unregistered w3id.org namespace at this stage. A neutral persistent identifier such as w3id.org may be considered later if the extension becomes community-maintained or moves toward standardization. Related MCP References This extension is intended to map onto the MCP Tool model documented in the official Model Context Protocol specification dated July 28, 2026: MCP specification: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28 MCP Tools section: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools For non-normative background on the intent and limits of MCP tool annotations, see: Tool Annotations as Risk Vocabulary: What Hints Can and Can't Do: https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-03-16-tool-annotations/ Canonical Schema The canonical schema entrypoint is schema/mcp-extension.yml . Implementations should load that file rather than importing individual record files directly. Normative Constraints Standard CWL remains authoritative for process execution and structural semantics. mcp:Tool must not duplicate CWL inputs or outputs. mcp:ToolAnnotations values are hints only. aliases may be preserved as extension metadata but are not a standard top-level MCP Tool field. Recommended Derivation Rules Name Precedence: mcp:Tool.name normalized CWL id Title Precedence: mcp:Tool.title CWL label normalized CWL id Description Precedence: mcp:Tool.description composed text from CWL doc , useWhen , and doNotUseWhen Annotations If present, mcp:Tool.annotations should map mechanically into MCP Tool annotations without reinterpretation. The aligned MCP 2026-07-28 annotation fields are: title readOnlyHint destructiveHint idempotentHint openWorldHint The MCP defaults are intentionally conservative when these hints are absent: readOnlyHint : false destructiveHint : true idempotentHint : false openWorldHint : true Validation With cwltool For this repository, cwltool is used to validate the underlying CWL document, while scripts/validate_with_mcp_schema.py adds repository-level checks for the mcp:Tool metadata structure. This keeps standard CWL validation delegated to cwltool and leaves the MCP extension constraints explicit and easy to evolve within this repository.
